results.summary_before: This project implements a 32x8 dual-port-read single-port-write RAM using D-type flip-flops, described by the author as a 'really bad implementation' due to its inefficiency. The RAM has two read ports (A and B) and one write port (A), with configurable features such as read buffering, write-through policy, and page selection via configuration bits latched on reset release. It is intended to be tested with standard Tiny Tapeout hardware and an RP2040, and a MicroPython interface is planned. The design is notable for its use of flip-flops instead of dedicated RAM blocks and its flexible read/write policies.

The design is a hardware implementation of a minimalist computer architecture, likely intended for educational purposes. No specific external hardware or test setup is described in the documentation.
